title: Tenant-scoped access & evidence automation for residency and retention
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Goal: Provide tenant-scoped access controls and automated evidence exports to satisfy data residency and retention requirements for regulated customers.

Scope:
- Implement tenant-scoped RBAC enforcement in the control plane with resource scoping and role inheritance for workspace, project, and model artifacts.
- Harden SAML mapping so identity provider groups can be mapped to tenant roles reliably across providers.
- Full SCIM provisioning flow for user lifecycle and group sync, with partial sync support for large orgs.
- Automated evidence/reporting pipeline that collects access events, attestation snapshots, and retention metadata into region-bound buckets for export to customer storage or audit archives.

Out of scope: Encrypted HSM key rotation UI (separate ticket), long-term archival cold storage management (future work).

Background: Several enterprise prospects require proof that access controls and retention policies are applied per-tenant and that audit artifacts (who had access, when, and what was retained) are exportable on demand. Current control plane enforces org-level roles but lacks strong tenant scoping for multi-tenant Dedicated and Private deployments and has manual evidence collection steps. This ticket combines engineering work to close the gap and automation for evidence exports used by compliance teams and customers.
acceptance_criteria: RBAC: roles can be created and bound at tenant and project scope; enforcement unit tests and e2e smoke tests pass in staging
SAML: group attribute mapping works for Okta and ADFS test IdPs; IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows both produce expected role assignments
SCIM: group membership changes provisioned by IdP reflect in Redwood within 2 minutes for delta syncs in small orgs; supports incremental sync for large orgs
Evidence pipeline: daily and on-demand exports produce a signed manifest (SHA256) containing access events and retention labels stored in region-tagged buckets
Privacy: evidence exports for a tenant only include artefacts from that tenant and are stored in the tenant's configured region
Retention: retention tags are attached to exported artifacts and the system enforces retention_period metadata for automated deletions in test harness
tasks: Design tenant RBAC model and migration plan
Add tenant_id column to policy store and migrate existing org policies with compatibility layer
Extend SAML mapping config to accept group-to-role templates and fallback rules
Implement SCIM incremental sync endpoint and add throttling for large org syncs
Build evidence collector agent that aggregates access events + attestation snapshots into per-tenant manifests
Add export connector to write artifacts to customer region-bound S3/GCS and generate signed manifests
Create e2e pipeline tests and compliance smoke dashboards
Coordinate with Security and Legal for audit schema and retention semantics
decisions: Adopt tenant-scoped RBAC (tenant_id first-class) to avoid leaky abstractions in Dedicated/Private deployments
Map IdP groups -> Redwood roles using a templated mapping configuration instead of hard-coded mappings to support customer heterogeneity
Evidence artifacts will be stored in region-tagged object stores (per tenant) and not duplicated globally to minimize residency risk
Use incremental SCIM syncs and a backfill job for initial migrations to reduce load on IdPs and our API gateways
tradeoffs: Adding tenant_id to the policy store increases query complexity and requires index tuning; chosen for clearer isolation rather than faster legacy queries
Generating signed manifests adds computation on export paths but is necessary for tamper-evidence for audits
Strong enforcement at request time may add a few ms to token checks; we will mitigate with local policy caches and async updates
